Relativizer choice: that, which or zero

Source: R/data.R
relativizers.Rd

The relativizer in restrictive relative clauses (the book that / which / 0 I read), 10 tokens from each of 240 texts, half spoken, half written. A three-way outcome; zero is impossible in subject relatives.

Usage

relativizers

Format

A tibble with 2400 rows and 6 columns:

text

Text ID, T001 to T240.

mode

"spoken" or "written".

token

Token number within the text, 1 to 10.

role

Role of the relativised noun in the clause, "subject" or "object".

antecedent_length

Length of the antecedent noun phrase in words.

relativizer

"that", "which" or "zero".

Source

data-raw/relativizers.R

Details

True model: multinomial logit with "that" as reference. Which: -1.6 + 1.4 * written + 0.25 * (antecedent_length - 2). Zero (object relatives only): 0.6 - 1.2 * written - 0.4 * (antecedent_length - 2). By-text intercepts with SD 0.5 for each.

Examples

table(relativizers$role, relativizers$relativizer)
#>          
#>           that which zero
#>   subject  869   463    0
#>   object   394   249  425
if (requireNamespace("nnet", quietly = TRUE)) {
  obj <- subset(relativizers, role == "object")
  obj$length_c <- obj$antecedent_length - 2
  m <- nnet::multinom(relativizer ~ mode + length_c, data = obj, trace = FALSE)
  round(coef(m), 2)
}
#>       (Intercept) modewritten length_c
#> which       -1.94        1.85     0.28
#> zero         0.62       -1.04    -0.33
